pattern-selector.why: the forces were one owner for the drift rule, a 10 second best-effort hook, and a mirrored installer copy that must still run; the chosen shape is an extracted shared module (no new pattern), with the rejected options (spawn esk-init --check, copy the code, force a version bump) recorded in ADR-0105.
pattern-selector.what: extracted the fingerprint and drift rule into skill-signature.mjs, imported by the installer and loaded best-effort by the emitter; recorded the options in ADR-0105.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

architectural-decision-records.why: changing what the session nudge reports and moving the drift rule to a shared owner is a significant decision; the choice, alternatives, cost, and limits are recorded in the same change.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0105 (MADR, accepted) and validated it with check_adr.sh through run-check.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the behavior is specified as executable scenarios for the operator and agent audiences across happy, edge, negative, and error paths, tagged, indexed, and logged.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added features/always-on/stale-mirror-nudge.feature (5 scenarios) and a step file driving the real emitter; regenerated the index and appended the coverage log; all 100 scenarios ran green.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the pure decision is unit tested directly and the emitter boundary is tested by spawning the real script against a sandboxed repo and home; the existing installer suite proves the extraction kept its behavior.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added drift cases to test/sync-nudge.test.mjs and emitter integration cases to test/emit-directive-nudge.test.mjs; esk-init.test.mjs passes unchanged.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the nudge is a check on install health, so the tests must fail when it is neutralized; seven hand-run mutants (no signature comparison, drifted names not passed, decideNudge ignoring drift, no time budget, hook-only command for content drift, custom target dropped, skipped scan read as in sync) each failed the suite, and the first also failed the BDD run.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: wrote discriminating unit, integration, and BDD cases and ran the seven mutants against them.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

skeptical-audit.why: the defect and the cost claim are backed by re-runnable observations (the real marker probe named the same 8 skills as esk-init --check, in 196 ms on one run) and the limits are named (a local edit inside the mirror is not nudged; a pre-signature marker nudges until one reconcile).
skeptical-audit.what: ran the probe against the real install read-only and stated the evidence and limits in ADR-0105.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review of the whole change ran against the four questions and is recorded in the append-only review log.
judge-arch.what: dispatched the review to a fresh subagent in two passes, fixed all 7 findings (3 medium, 4 low), and appended the review entry.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

release-deployment-safety.why: the change alters what runs at every session start for anyone on the user-level hook; it is additive and best-effort (a missing module or bad marker means no nudge), a marker without a skills record behaves exactly as before, and the existing ESK_NUDGE_DISABLE switch turns it off without a redeploy.
release-deployment-safety.what: kept the drift check behind a dynamic import inside the existing best-effort try, and left the kill switch in place.
quotes: Dark-launch: ship the code off, turn it on for internal users, then 1 percent

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: the drift rule had one implementation inside the installer; the emitter now reuses it through one shared module instead of a copy, the simplest shape that meets the requirement.
enterprise-architecture-standards.what: extracted signatureOf, mirrorDrift, and skillNamesIn into skill-signature.mjs and made esk-init's --check use mirrorDrift.
quotes: Simplicity that meets the real requirement is a core principle, not a shortcut.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: no auth, session, network, or secret is touched. The only new input is the user's own local install marker, read to locate a folder that is then only hashed, never written or executed; the names printed come from the repo's own skill folders, and the output is control-character cleaned by the existing emitter.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data; the change reads skill files and a local install record and writes only the existing nudge counter.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service or endpoint is added; the hook's latency was measured (196 ms) against its 10 second limit and recorded in ADR-0105.

arch-encode.why: no greppable architectural mistake was caught that needs a new arch-gate forbid rule; the one duplication risk was removed by the extraction itself.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no user interface; the only output is a plain-text SessionStart context string.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or device surface; these are Node hooks and an installer.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no interactive surface; the nudge text is plain language that names the stale skills and the exact fix command.
